Daily Brief

The day's news was dominated by the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO following pressure from President Trump, a move that added nearly $1 trillion to the company's market value but drew criticism from lawmakers concerned about national security given Huang's alleged relationship with a suspected Chinese spy [BBC, Le Monde, Financial Times]. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte pledged to defend against threats in space after German intelligence reports indicated Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite dubbed 'Sputnik-S' within 60 days [BBC]. In China, Shanghai's powerful Communist Party Secretary Chen Jining was placed under investigation for 'severe violations of discipline and laws,' marking one of the highest-profile targets of Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign ahead of the 2027 Party Congress [The Hindu, Financial Times, Nikkei Asia]. Ukraine continued expanding its long-range strike capabilities, with President Zelenskyy confirming responsibility for drone attacks on Russian vessels in Libya and the Gulf of Finland, raising concerns among allies about escalation [The Guardian, ABC Australia]. Meanwhile, the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled that Senegal won the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations, ending an 11-month legal dispute with Morocco over the chaotic final [RFI].

03 Geopolitics

Shanghai Communist Party Chief Chen Jining Placed Under Corruption Investigation

  • Chen Jining, 62, Shanghai's top Communist Party leader and Politburo member, was announced to be under investigation for 'suspected severe violations of discipline and laws'
  • Chen was widely expected to receive a prominent national role at the 2027 Party Congress where Xi Jinping is set to begin a fourth term
  • Chen previously served as president of Xi's alma mater Tsinghua University and as Beijing mayor before his Shanghai appointment in 2022
  • Politburo members are rarely investigated, with only half a dozen such cases historically

04 Conflict

Ukraine Claims Responsibility for Drone Strikes on Russian Ships in Libya and Gulf of Finland

  • Ukraine confirmed using seven naval drones launched from a mothership to strike two Russian vessels in Benghazi, Libya, sinking the corvette Merkury
  • President Zelenskyy also claimed responsibility for Saturday's drone strike on the cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland
  • The Libya operation occurred 1,500 miles from the frontline, representing a significant geographic expansion of Ukraine's strike capabilities
  • Russia called the attacks 'dangerous escalation' while Norway urged caution; Finland, Estonia and Russian vessels conducted joint rescue operations

05 Society

Court of Arbitration for Sport Declares Senegal 2025 Africa Cup of Nations Champions

  • CAS ruled in favor of Senegal, ending an 11-month legal dispute over the January 2026 final in which Senegal beat Morocco 1-0
  • Morocco had appealed after Senegalese players walked off the field without referee permission following a controversial penalty decision
  • CAF's appeals panel had initially sided with Morocco in March, declaring Senegal had forfeited by walking off
  • The ruling ends a saga that significantly damaged the reputation of Africa's most prestigious national team tournament
